theorems.name: msc_applicable_requirements_and_policy
theorems.statement: An MSC implementation provides the functions needed by its selected capabilities and satisfies every applicable threshold requirement or its stated objective alternative, together with applicable CNSS and local policy; CP requirements take precedence over conflicting local policy.

theorems.name: msc_validated_configuration_and_modification
theorems.statement: Every Solution Component uses its NIAP-certified evaluated configuration, and an actual modification has the NIAP statement required by the CSfC PMO. Consultation with the vendor and NIAP continuity process is recommended for a proposed modification.

theorems.name: msc_listed_product_eligibility
theorems.statement: Selected VPN Gateways, MACsec Devices, firewalls, and Authentication Servers belong to their specified CSfC product lists; selecting the optional IPS capability requires the IPS list, and NIAP certification alone does not establish list eligibility.

theorems.name: msc_implementation_diversity
theorems.statement: Inner and Outer Encryption Components satisfy manufacturer or NSA-approved product independence, use different operating systems beyond service-pack or version differences, and use independent cryptographic libraries; any Gray Firewall also satisfies the specified independence relationship with Inner Encryption Components.

theorems.name: msc_physically_distinct_security_components
theorems.statement: Inner and Outer Encryption Components use distinct physical devices, and the required firewalls and encryption components use separate devices with no device serving more than one of the specified functions.

theorems.name: msc_supply_chain_assessment
theorems.statement: Every selected component undergoes the organization’s AO-approved Product Supply Chain Threat Assessment so that mitigations are determined for its intended application.

theorems.name: msc_nested_layer_protection
theorems.statement: Every protected data flow across the untrusted Black Network passes through independent Inner then Outer encryption and the reverse decryption sequence using the IPsec/MACsec pairings in Table 1; each layer terminates on its matching encryption components, and Outer MACsec configurations are limited to point-to-point use.

theorems.name: msc_security_level_connectivity
theorems.statement: Red Networks communicate through MSC only within the same security level, and Inner VPN Gateways authenticate and establish tunnels only for Red Networks of that level; multiple levels can share Outer infrastructure while each Red or included unclassified network retains its own Inner Encryption Component and applicable Red-network protections.

theorems.name: msc_gray_network_classification_boundary
theorems.statement: The Solution Owner or a trusted third party controls the Red and Gray Networks, and the MSC design is inapplicable if the classification authority classifies exposed Gray information that the design does not protect with two encryption layers.

theorems.name: msc_independently_managed_sites
theorems.statement: In the independently managed design, each site administers its own Encryption Components without management traffic crossing the Black Network, maintains interoperable peers, and provides the appropriate cross-site CA signing and revocation information or shared CAK for each communicating encryption relationship.

theorems.name: msc_centrally_managed_sites
theorems.statement: In the central-management design, the central personnel administer and key the sites with interoperable components, separate Inner and Outer CA functions, central CAs and an AS for certificate-based MACsec, and the required protection of management traffic across sites; enterprise CAs are preferred when available.

theorems.name: msc_security_level_key_and_management_separation
theorems.statement: Distinct Red security levels have separate CAs, CAKs, and management devices for their Inner Encryption Components so that components at different levels cannot mutually authenticate; same-level designs may elect the additional filtering controls described for multiple levels.

theorems.name: msc_gray_firewall_path_coverage
theorems.statement: All Gray-network paths between Inner Encryption Components for different security levels, and the specified paths between Gray management services and lower-level Inner components, include Gray Firewalls that block the prohibited flows; Outer filtering remains required even when standalone Gray Firewalls are present.

theorems.name: msc_gray_addressing_for_level_filtering
theorems.statement: Gray addresses and address ranges distinguish security levels so that the specified packet filters can admit only intended same-level Inner peers and reject cross-level paths.

theorems.name: msc_macsec_encapsulation
theorems.statement: Inner MACsec traffic, and MACsec traffic crossing an IP network, receives encapsulation before Outer encryption without premature MACsec decryption; an unsupported built-in encapsulation feature requires a correctly connected standalone encapsulator, and its applicable Solution Component obligations are resolved explicitly from the conflicting source passages.

theorems.name: msc_macsec_optional_clear_vlan_and_xpn
theorems.statement: A MACsec implementation may expose the VLAN ID tag and may use XPN when its device supports those features, while retaining the other applicable MACsec protection requirements.

theorems.name: msc_mutual_device_authentication_and_npe
theorems.statement: Inner peers and Outer peers mutually authenticate using the method appropriate to VPN or MACsec, and every issued device authentication certificate for those components is a Non-Person Entity certificate.

theorems.name: msc_cnss_algorithm_policy
theorems.statement: The solution satisfies the §2 algorithm-policy choices for confidentiality, authentication, key establishment, integrity, and objective software/firmware signing, respecting the listed threshold and objective alternatives and the detailed protocol tables.

theorems.name: msc_ipsec_algorithm_profile_choice
theorems.statement: Each VPN tunnel follows either the threshold CNSA 1.0 proposal profile or the corresponding CNSA 2.0 objective profile, whose initial IKE_SA_INIT uses a size-bounded CNSA 1.0 exchange and whose encrypted IKE_INTERMEDIATE uses ML-KEM-1024 with the specified IKE extensions and Table 7 algorithms outside the initial exchange.

theorems.name: msc_vpn_certificate_authentication
theorems.statement: VPN Gateways authenticate during IKE using unique device certificates and the corresponding CA chain through its trust anchor, reject revoked or expired certificates, and either do not use preinstalled default/self-signed/proprietary certificates or remove them under the objective alternative.

theorems.name: msc_vpn_private_key_confinement
theorems.statement: A VPN Gateway private key is inaccessible through an interface, and the optional objective Mandatory Access Control policy permits only that VPN Gateway to access its key.

theorems.name: msc_ike_version_and_encryption_modes
theorems.statement: Every VPN Gateway uses IKEv2 and selects a permitted IKE encryption mode and a permitted ESP encryption mode: CBC at threshold or GCM at objective, with HMAC integrity when ESP CBC is selected.

theorems.name: msc_vpn_sa_lifetimes_and_reauthentication
theorems.statement: Every VPN Gateway configures an IKE SA lifetime of at most 24 hours and an ESP SA lifetime of at most 8 hours, and reauthenticates its tunnel peer before rekeying an IKE SA.

theorems.name: msc_macsec_authentication_choice_and_as
theorems.statement: MACsec peers authenticate using either PSK CAKs or certificate-based EAP-TLS; the certificate branch uses an AS for mutual device-certificate authentication, each MACsec device acts as supplicant and authenticator, and the AS obeys the stated one-site and Red/Gray network connection restrictions.

theorems.name: msc_macsec_encryption_and_key_wrap
theorems.statement: MACsec Devices use 256-bit AES Key Wrap for key distribution and 256-bit AES GCM for MACsec protection with the algorithms specified in Table 9.

theorems.name: msc_macsec_eap_tls_profile_choice
theorems.statement: Certificate-authenticated MACsec Devices and their AS use either the Table 10 CNSA 1.0 EAP-TLS suite or the objective Table 11 CNSA 2.0 suite, with ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, and TLS 1.3 in the CNSA 2.0 branch.

theorems.name: msc_macsec_key_generation_and_server
theorems.statement: MACsec CKNs come from an NSA-approved KGS and are at least 16 bytes. The applicable CAK-generation constraint remains provisional for the EAP-TLS branch because the source states both MSK derivation and KGS generation of all CAKs; the PSK branch uses the stated approved-KGS generation. Each pair sets the prescribed key-server values with the central site serving when present, and fallback CAKs are disabled.

theorems.name: msc_macsec_protection_parameters
theorems.statement: MACsec Devices enable MKA data-delay protection, set lifetime and hello timeouts to 6.0 and 2.0 seconds, set the replay window to 2 or the lowest value possible for the Black Network, encrypt all external data traffic, set confidentiality offset to zero, and operate in must-secure mode.

theorems.name: msc_inner_tunnel_no_bypass
theorems.statement: Inner VPN Gateways use ESP tunnel mode with an associated IP tunneling protocol; Inner Encryption Components never bypass encryption from Red to Gray or decryption from Gray to Red and never permit split tunneling, using Mandatory Access Control in each selected objective branch.

theorems.name: msc_outer_tunnel_no_bypass
theorems.statement: Outer VPN Gateways use ESP tunnel mode; Outer Encryption Components accept already-encrypted Gray traffic except permitted control-plane traffic, never bypass encryption to Black or decryption from Black, and never permit split tunneling, using Mandatory Access Control in each selected objective branch.

theorems.name: msc_encryption_component_routing_limits
theorems.statement: Outer Encryption Components do not implement routing protocols or routing functionality as stated in the prose, while permitted firewall infrastructure supplies dynamic routing; Inner Encryption Components do not switch or route for other Encryption Components.

theorems.name: msc_transec_conditions
theorems.statement: TRANSEC is enabled under the applicable Public-Internet and MACsec-to-Outer-Firewall conditions once the conflicting prose and objective-table requirement strength are resolved explicitly.

theorems.name: msc_packet_size_configuration
theorems.statement: Gray Firewall/Encryption Component external packet sizes satisfy the required IPv4 MTU or IPv6 PMTU configuration, and the optional Inner interface objective sizes packets or frames with the Black Network and Outer Component limits in view.

theorems.name: msc_outer_firewall_placement
theorems.statement: An MSC solution using an untrusted Black network such as the Public Internet places an Outer Firewall between that network and the Outer Encryption Component, with the stated internal and external connections.

theorems.name: msc_boundary_interface_filtering
theorems.statement: Outer VPN Black interfaces permit IKE/ESP and approved control traffic, Outer MACsec Black interfaces permit MACsec PDUs and approved control traffic, and Inner Gray interfaces permit the listed tunnel/control protocols in both directions. Inner Red interfaces permit only addresses and ports associated with Red services. A required Outer Firewall applies its protocol allowlist, with its external interface using the local Outer Encryption Component as the permitted destination and its internal interface using that local component as the permitted source, subject to the stated control-plane allowances. Packets leaving the Outer Encryption Component make connections only to the remote Outer Encryption Component or other intended device.

theorems.name: msc_minimal_interface_exposure
theorems.statement: Each Solution Component restricts every network interface to the smallest possible address ranges, ports, and protocols and disables every unused network interface.

theorems.name: msc_outer_third_party_services
theorems.statement: Every service or feature enabling an Outer Encryption Component to contact a third-party server is blocked at threshold or disabled at objective.

theorems.name: msc_ip_header_and_multicast_filtering
theorems.statement: Outer Encryption Components drop external multicast, VPN Gateways admit only the specified IPv4 Protocol or IPv6 Next Header values, and the selected IPv4 Outer-IPsec objective drops packets containing IP options.

theorems.name: msc_outer_gray_interface_policy
theorems.statement: Outer Gray interfaces admit the specified same-level Inner tunnel traffic, approved management/control traffic, and conditional revocation HTTP; restrict management initiation to Gray AWs except Outer logging/authentication; enforce source reachability and peer addressing; and deny traffic outside PF-8, PF-13, PF-15, and PF-19.

theorems.name: msc_gray_firewall_allowlist
theorems.statement: A required Gray Firewall permits the listed same-level tunnel, revocation HTTP, physical-management-port, and control-plane traffic; enforces peer address and source-reachability restrictions; denies traffic outside the enumerated exceptions; and blocks traffic between Inner VPN Gateways of different classification levels.

theorems.name: msc_control_plane_policy_and_services
theorems.statement: Control-plane services reside inside the relevant encryption layer; unapproved protocols are blocked or disabled; necessary standards-conformant Layer 2 protocols are permitted, Layer 3 defaults to disabled unless AO policy allows it, and Red/Gray multicast and existing routing protocols follow their stated AO conditions. Networks may independently select IPv4 or IPv6, and appropriate protocols may be selected where the CP does not specify one.

theorems.name: msc_trusted_time_synchronization
theorems.statement: Inner Encryption Components and Red Management Services synchronize to a trusted Red time source, while Outer Encryption Components, Gray Management Services, and any Gray Firewall synchronize to a trusted source in the Gray Management Network.

theorems.name: msc_defaults_dns_and_boot_configuration
theorems.statement: Solution Components change or remove default access-control values, specify DNS server addresses or disable DNS services, and disable automatic remote boot-time configuration; the optional objective disables network-device DNS lookup.

theorems.name: msc_layered_administrative_separation
theorems.statement: Each component has adequate AW administration, with at least one Red AW and one Gray AW; Inner/Red and Outer/Gray management use their respective networks and distinct AWs, dedicated management interfaces, and the stated physical, cryptographic, and ACL separation from data traffic; Gray Management has no direct connection to NIPRNet or another unclassified network not dedicated to CSfC administration.

theorems.name: msc_dedicated_and_hardened_aws
theorems.statement: Physical AWs and AW virtual machines use the stated dedicated hardware/VM boundaries, reside in protected facilities, exclude prohibited functions and non-CSfC uses, follow vendor and organizational hardening/patching policy, and power off when unused.

theorems.name: msc_secure_management_transport
theorems.statement: Solution Components are managed securely through an AW over an NSA-approved remote solution or locally; management addresses are minimized, network management uses the listed secure protocols, direct physical local management has its stated exception, and Black-network management receives two approved encryption layers with the local LAN/VLAN qualification retained.

theorems.name: msc_administrator_authentication
theorems.statement: Security Administrators authenticate before administrative functions, using CNSA certificates under the objective alternative; each AW administrator has unique credentials without group accounts, and the optional NIST SP 800-63 objective applies when selected.

theorems.name: msc_authorized_initial_provisioning
theorems.statement: The Solution Owner identifies authorized Security Administrators, who provision components out of band in a secured area before first use, initiate the required CSRs, deliver them to the appropriate Inner or Outer CA, and install unique signed certificates with their chains; AWs interacting with the Outer VPN CA reside on Gray.

theorems.name: msc_personnel_clearance
theorems.statement: Security Administrators, Auditors, and Integrators hold the highest protected-data clearance, subject to the stated Black Network Administrator exception, and Outer administrators meet the highest Red classification at the Outer Component’s site.

theorems.name: msc_siem_collection_alerting_and_protection
theorems.statement: Deployed Red and Gray SIEM functions collect the stated component logs and flow data and provide the specified alerts. Log transport is recommended to use SSHv2, TLS 1.2 or later, IPsec, or MACsec encryption. Gray functions may move to a Red SIEM through an approved CDS, and a Gray SIEM is optional.

theorems.name: msc_cross_domain_solution_conditions
theorems.statement: Any CDS used in the solution adheres to DoDI 8540.01 and the DISN Connection Process Guide and is on the National Cross Domain Strategy Management Office CDS Baseline.

theorems.name: msc_physical_protection_access_and_disposal
theorems.statement: Solution Components other than the stated Outer Firewall exception receive the highest required classified physical protection, only authorized cleared or escorted personnel gain physical access, MACsec configuration copies receive CAK-level protection, and components are disposed of as classified unless AO-approved declassification procedures apply.

theorems.name: msc_shared_outer_interface_topology
theorems.statement: Inner Encryption Components sharing an Outer Encryption Component are arranged in parallel, and that Outer Component has a unique physical internal interface for each Red Network without VLAN trunking of multiple enclaves.

theorems.name: msc_site_interoperability
theorems.statement: Every pair of sites that needs to communicate selects interoperable components for each tunnel, with interoperability testing recommended despite product-list eligibility.

theorems.name: msc_combined_cp_firewalls
theorems.statement: When MSC is combined with another CSfC solution, a required Gray Firewall is included and any Inner Firewall requirements imposed by a combined data-in-transit/end-user-device CP are followed; the standalone MSC CP does not itself require an Inner Firewall.

theorems.name: msc_approved_red_egress_paths
theorems.statement: Every physical path leaving a Red Network uses a conforming MSC solution or an AO-approved data-in-transit protection solution, allowing the stated coexistence of an NSA-certified product path and a CP-conforming CSfC path.

theorems.name: msc_patches_virus_updates_and_tempest
theorems.statement: Solution Components receive virus updates as required by policy and the AO, security-critical patches are tested then applied according to policy and this CP, local policy specifies patch installation, and components comply with local TEMPEST policy.

theorems.name: msc_inventory_and_baseline_configuration
theorems.statement: Every hardware component is tracked by the AO-approved inventory process as part of a CSfC solution, and the Security Administrator maintains a baseline configuration available to the Auditor.

theorems.name: msc_procurement_purpose_nondisclosure
theorems.statement: Acquisition and procurement documentation omits the equipment purpose, including its use to protect classified information.

theorems.name: msc_compliance_audits
theorems.statement: The Solution Owner permits and fully cooperates with NSA-authorized compliance audits, the AO ensures an annual audit against the latest CP as part of re-registration, and the AO receives and reviews the results.

theorems.name: msc_registration_and_version_updates
theorems.statement: Before operational use the customer obtains NSA registration approval and submits the complete registration package and AO compliance matrix, then renews annually and updates changed registration information; new-version compliance follows an explicitly resolved deadline preserving both the table and §13.3 statements.

theorems.name: msc_audit_log_retention_and_continuity
theorems.statement: Audit data is retained for at least one year, remaining capacity is assessed quarterly, frequent backups occur, incident-reporting guidance is documented, and the organization maintains an audit continuity plan covering capacity warnings, long-term offload, overflow response, and power events.

theorems.name: msc_infrastructure_authentication_choice
theorems.statement: Infrastructure components use either threshold passwords containing at least 112 random bits or the objective authentication service on their respective network/domain, with an approved password generator recommended for the password branch.

theorems.name: msc_incident_reporting
theorems.statement: For every reportable incident under RP-3 through RP-15, the Solution Owner reports the confirmed incident within 24 hours of detection through the stated NSA channel and supplies at least all RP-2 fields, treating unexplained activity as malicious unless known non-malicious and preserving the Black-connectivity exception.

theorems.name: msc_separation_of_personnel_roles
theorems.statement: Different people perform Security Administrator and Auditor roles, different administrators manage Inner/Red and Outer/Gray components, and optional Mandatory Access Control role definitions apply when selected; customers may also require Red/Gray separation among Integrator personnel.

theorems.name: msc_training_and_hardware_inspection
theorems.statement: Security Administrators and Auditors meet local IA training requirements, and administrators periodically inspect infrastructure hardware for tampering or unauthorized physical changes.

theorems.name: msc_predisposal_key_revocation
theorems.statement: Security Administrators initiate the certificate-revocation or CAK-destruction process before disposal of any Solution Component.

theorems.name: msc_security_administrator_duties
theorems.statement: Security Administrators maintain, monitor, and control solution security, apply critical updates, document/report incidents, support integration and maintenance logistics with necessary escorts, defend auxiliary network devices, and maintain CP-version compliance according to GD-11.

theorems.name: msc_auditor_duties_and_access
theorems.statement: The Auditor reviews administrator actions and audit events for compromise, manages audit log data, documents and reports incidents, develops and reports a System Audit Capability Survey, and is authorized access only to Inner and Outer administration components.

theorems.name: msc_integrator_permitted_duties
theorems.statement: A customer may engage an external Integrator to implement the CP, with the possible duties of acquiring products, configuring the solution, documenting/testing/maintaining it, and responding to incidents, subject to the applicable CP obligations.

theorems.name: msc_ao_authorization_and_lifecycle_control
theorems.statement: The customer obtains security assessment and authorization using the referenced risk information and provides the results and NSA Risk Assessment to the AO. A customer wanting a solution variant contacts its NSA External Engagement Representative to determine how to obtain approval. The AO verifies proper implementation, maintains lifecycle configuration/update control, and ensures that certificate/CAK revocation information is updated on all Solution Components after compromise.

theorems.name: msc_solution_testing_and_evidence
theorems.statement: The implementing organization tests every security feature and operational capability, executes all Testing Annex tests, documents the baseline and discrepancies, uses Black- and Gray-Box tests, checks that local requirements do not impair security, retains test artifacts, and delivers the final report to the AO, with two-person testing recommended.

theorems.name: msc_software_firmware_signature_choice
theorems.statement: When the software/firmware signing objective is selected, every Solution Component uses one of the Table 2 approved algorithms and its stated parameters; one permitted algorithm is sufficient for the requirement.

theorems.name: msc_redundant_component_permission
theorems.statement: An implementation may add parallel redundant encryption components or multiple compliant firewalls for failover or throughput only while every added security component meets its applicable CP requirements; the shown infrastructure router carries only the explicitly stated CP scope.

theorems.name: msc_additional_control_permissions
theorems.statement: An implementation may add the stated risk-reducing controls, including a screening router on the Black Network; the router is outside the MSC Solution boundary and optional annex components receive only the scope expressly stated by the source.

theorems.name: msc_cp_user_legal_undertaking
theorems.statement: Use of the CP is associated with the source’s disclaimer and user undertaking to hold harmless and indemnify the U.S. Government, its agents, and employees for the listed claims; any formal representation must preserve the stated scope and receive legal-domain review.
